creator: Unknown (vector reconstruction)
rights_holder: Public domain — simple flag design/common information
license_exact: Public domain — copyright-ineligible common-property design (Commons PD-ineligible)
attribution_text: Flag of Belgium as described by the 1831 Constitution; vector reconstruction via Wikimedia Commons, public domain/ineligible for copyright.
notes: Commons file page captions this as the Belgian flag according to the 1831 Constitution and dates it 7 February 1831. It describes the constitutional order of black, yellow and red vertical colours; the file is a vector reconstruction, not the original 1831 cloth. The horizontal temporary-government flag of 1830 is a different earlier form and must not be substituted for the 1836 kingdom. The flag design is marked public domain/ineligible for copyright; legal restrictions on official insignia may still apply.

creator: Fornax (vector reconstruction)
license_exact: Public domain — author release (PD-self); Commons also identifies PD-Bolivia and PD-ineligible
attribution_text: Fornax, Flag of Bolivia (1826–1851).svg, released to the public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
notes: Commons file page identifies the design as Bolivia 1831–1851 / 1826–1851; this interval covers 1 January 1836. It is a reconstruction by Fornax with public-domain release, and Commons additionally marks PD-Bolivia and PD-ineligible. The file is an official insignia; reuse restrictions independent of copyright may apply. Do not confuse with the 1831–1851 Bandera Mayor or with the separate Peru–Bolivian Confederation flag of 1836–1839; this simple national flag entry is the 1826–1851 form.

creator: Orange Tuesday
attribution_text: Orange Tuesday, Flag of Paraguay (1826–1842).svg, released into the public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
notes: Commons file page identifies the design as the flag of Paraguay from 1826 to 1842 and records the author's public-domain release. Flags of the World history page says a new flag was introduced in 1826 and the tricolour remained an alternate; after Francia's death in 1840, garrisons used his blue flag until 1842. A 1830–1842 horizontal tricolour is documented as an alternate, while the official 1826 flag was the blue field with a white six-pointed star. Use the 1826–1842 blue-star design as the principal state flag; do not mistake the alternate tricolour for the official flag.

creator: Ysangkok (vector reconstruction)
attribution_text: Ysangkok, Flag of Muscat.svg, released into the public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
notes: Commons file depicts the plain red flag of the Sultanate of Muscat and is public domain by author release. Oman's Foreign Ministry says the old Omani flag was all red; FOTW reports the plain red flag continued until 17 December 1970 and discusses the 1820 treaty context, but notes that 19th-century Gulf red flags and the distinction between Muscat and interior Oman can be ambiguous. The modern state name Sultanate of Muscat and Oman was used after the 1820 union. Use as a historical reference with medium confidence; do not infer a precise 1820 adoption date or assume the flag represented the inland Imamate at all times.
